rich_summary: Bhishma recounts to Yudhishthira the famous tale of King Sivi (here associated with Vrishadarbha) to illustrate the supreme duty of protecting those who seek refuge. A pigeon fleeing a hawk takes shelter on the king’s lap. When the hawk demands its natural prey, the king refuses to abandon one who has sought protection and instead offers his own flesh equal to the pigeon’s weight. Piece by piece he cuts his body, yet the pigeon outweighs the flesh until the king finally climbs onto the scale himself. His uncompromising righteousness shakes the cosmos, and the gods appear, honor him, and grant him heaven. Bhishma uses the story to teach that a ruler’s highest virtue is steadfast protection of dependents. The chapter then turns to another principle of kingship: honoring learned Brahmanas, whose spiritual power sustains and stabilizes the kingdom.

highlight_spans.why: The hawk’s argument about natural law and royal power frames the moral dilemma between compassion and the ordained order of nature.
The king declares his unbreakable vow never to abandon one who has sought his protection, establishing the central ethical commitment.
The dramatic moment when the king begins cutting flesh from his own body while the palace erupts in grief highlights the emotional and moral intensity of his sacrifice.
The climax where the king, reduced to a skeleton, mounts the scale himself, demonstrating absolute dedication to his promise.
Bhishma states the lesson: a ruler who protects dependents and those seeking refuge gains great happiness and merit.
The transition to Bhishma’s teaching that honoring learned Brahmanas is the foremost duty of a king, expanding the chapter’s instruction on righteous rule.

top_scenes.scene_text: King Sivi sits on a throne holding a trembling pigeon on his lap while a hawk confronts him, the royal court watching the tense moral dispute.
The king cutting flesh from his own body and placing it on a balance scale against the pigeon as queens and courtiers cry out in horror.
The skeletal but resolute king climbing onto the scale as gods appear in the sky, flowers and nectar raining down from the heavens.
